Extract abundances in the shared taxonomic analysis view

Source: R/analysis-data.R
tidy_abundance.Rd

tidy_abundance() returns one row per taxon and sample. When a centralized model is defined, taxa are aggregated through its selected taxonomic rank, using the same identities as differential-abundance results. Without a centralized model, the stored features are returned without aggregation.

Usage

tidy_abundance(rec, taxa_ids = NULL, transform = "identity", metadata = NULL)

Arguments

rec

A Recipe or PrepRecipe object.

taxa_ids

Optional character vector of taxon identifiers to retain. IDs refer to the shared analysis view, not absorbed features. NULL retains every analysis taxon; character(0) returns no rows. Output keeps analysis taxon order rather than selector order.

transform

Either "identity" for stored abundances or "compositional" for within-sample fractions. Fractions use all shared analysis taxa as their denominator before taxa_ids selection. Zero-depth samples have missing fractions and produce a warning.

metadata

Character vector of sample metadata columns to include. NULL includes every column; character(0) includes none. Supply the original, unprefixed column names.

Value

A tibble with taxa_id, taxa, sample_id, abundance, complete namespaced taxonomy and selected namespaced sample metadata. taxa uses the configured taxonomic label, or feature IDs when no single rank is configured. Sample metadata types are preserved. Rows follow analysis taxon order, then sample order.

Details

This is a descriptive view of the data currently stored in the recipe. A prepared recipe includes common preprocessing and the shared model cohort; an unprepared recipe does not execute its configured steps. Neither view reproduces method-specific filtering, rarefaction or transformations, or adjusted model predictions.

Taxonomic columns are prefixed with taxonomy_ and sample metadata columns with metadata_, so annotations cannot overwrite identifiers or abundances. Full lineage through the selected rank is retained; lower ranks removed by aggregation remain missing. Taxa sharing a label but not a lineage retain distinct taxa_id values.

Examples

data(metaHIV_phy)
rec <- recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  add_model(~ RiskGroup2, targets = "RiskGroup2", tax_level = "Genus")
abundances <- tidy_abundance(rec, metadata = "RiskGroup2")
head(abundances)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 12
#>   taxa_id taxa              sample_id abundance taxonomy_Kingdom taxonomy_Phylum
#>   <chr>   <chr>             <chr>         <dbl> <chr>            <chr>          
#> 1 Otu_1   Methanobrevibact… Sample_1…      2538 Archaea          Euryarchaeota  
#> 2 Otu_1   Methanobrevibact… Sample_1…         0 Archaea          Euryarchaeota  
#> 3 Otu_1   Methanobrevibact… Sample_1…      9026 Archaea          Euryarchaeota  
#> 4 Otu_1   Methanobrevibact… Sample_1…     12049 Archaea          Euryarchaeota  
#> 5 Otu_1   Methanobrevibact… Sample_1…     22126 Archaea          Euryarchaeota  
#> 6 Otu_1   Methanobrevibact… Sample_1…     15374 Archaea          Euryarchaeota  
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: taxonomy_Class <chr>, taxonomy_Order <chr>,
#> #   taxonomy_Family <chr>, taxonomy_Genus <chr>, taxonomy_Species <chr>,
#> #   metadata_RiskGroup2 <chr>

fractions <- tidy_abundance(
  rec, transform = "compositional", metadata = character(0)
)
